summary: Confirmed DONE. Electron main no longer does any synchronous log I/O. desktop-main.log and server-child.log are both AsyncRotatingFileSink (held append handle, one writev per batch, fs.promises rotation). A captured console chunk is one writeBatch instead of 3 appendFileSync calls. LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES dropped from 10 to 3. In desktop mode the backend writes its own logfmt server.log through a batched async sink, which Diagnostics tails, and Electron stops writing backend output to disk once the backend serves. The user's live log dir shows it working: server-child.log gets one '---- backend serving; its output continues in server.log ----' marker per session, and server.log has been written since Oct 12 at about 150 KB/day. One small defect: PR #710 cut maxFiles from 10 to 3 and, in the same change, replaced the readdir-based overflow prune with a probe of only maxFiles+1..maxFiles+3. Backups .7 to .10 left by the old depth are never deleted on upgraded installs.

evidence.note: initializePackagedLogging creates desktopLogSink and backendLogSink as AsyncRotatingFileSink. No sync RotatingFileSink is used anywhere outside tests (git grep).
writeDesktopStreamChunk builds [prefix, buffer, optional newline] and calls desktopLogSink.writeBatch once, so one writev per console chunk.
AsyncRotatingFileSink opens its handle lazily, appends with handle.writev, rotates through fs.promises rename/rm, and serializes writes through writeTail.

LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES = 3 (was 10 at f1be4abc7). Rotation keeps current + .1..3, so 4 x 10 MiB per log and 80 MiB for both logs, down from about 220 MiB (the auditor's 60 MiB undercounts the current file).
captureBackendOutput sends each chunk to BackendOutputCapture.push(buffer, readiness.ready). The readiness detector and startup outputTail are only fed while !readiness.ready.

BackendOutputCapture writes to server-child.log only before ready. After that it writes one 'backend serving' marker and keeps a 16 KB in-memory tail, which is written only in recordUnexpectedExit (main.ts handleChildGone, skipped while quitting or on an expected exit).

In desktop mode the server also pushes makeServerLogFileLogger({filePath: config.serverLogPath}): logfmt, 250 ms / 64-line batches, a 4 MB pending cap that drops lines and counts them, and a 10 MiB x 3 AsyncRotatingFileSink. Logger.consolePretty is still installed, so backend output still goes over the stdout pipe into Electron main after ready, where it only feeds the 16 KB tail (microbench: about 0.46 us per 228-byte chunk).
readFailureLogTail tails config.serverLogPath (logs/server.log), and failureFromLogLine handles the logfmt prefix. The Diagnostics source that used to be dead is now populated.

Defect: pruneOverflowBackups only probes maxFiles+1..maxFiles+OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT (3), which is .4..6 for the desktop sinks. Both this and the 10->3 maxFiles cut landed in 60633eff3. The old sync and async sinks used readdir and removed every suffix above maxFiles.

Live check: server-child.log has 15 'backend serving' markers, the latest session stops right after 'Listening on', and server.log (796 lines since 2026-10-12) exists. No .4+ desktop backups exist on this machine, so the prune gap does not affect it.

fixDefects: Low severity: on installs that had rotated deeper than .6 under the old maxFiles=10, desktop-main.log.7..10 and server-child.log.7..10 are never pruned (packages/shared/src/logging.ts:307-322 probes only indices 4..6 when maxFiles=3). That leaves up to 8 x 10 MiB = 80 MiB of static orphaned files, which partly undoes the finding's '~140 MiB lower worst-case disk cap' for upgraded users. Minor, and inherent to the async design: a line logged right before an immediate app.exit (e.g. 'second instance refused' at apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4639-4640) may be lost now that the write is async. Not a perf defect. Also: the sync RotatingFileSink in packages/shared/src/logging.ts:34 is only used by apps/desktop/src/rotatingFileSink.test.ts and could be deleted.
implementationSketch: Prune gap: in packages/shared/src/logging.ts, add an optional `pruneBackupsUpTo?: number` option to AsyncRotatingFileSinkOptions (default maxFiles + OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT). Have pruneOverflowBackups probe indices maxFiles+1..max(that, pruneBackupsUpTo), still with exact-path rm (force), never readdir. In apps/desktop/src/main.ts initializePackagedLogging, pass `pruneBackupsUpTo: 10` (the legacy LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES, kept as a named constant like LEGACY_LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES with a comment) to both desktop sinks. A simpler alternative is raising OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT to 8, which costs a few extra async rm calls per sink at startup. Test: extend packages/shared/src/logging.test.ts 'prunes backups left by a deeper rotation' with .7 and .10 (+ .gz) files and maxFiles 3 / pruneBackupsUpTo 10, then assert only .1..3 remain and readdir is not called. Optional cleanup: delete the sync RotatingFileSink and move or delete apps/desktop/src/rotatingFileSink.test.ts. Optional and not worth it at about 150 KB/day: in packaged desktop mode, drop Logger.consolePretty after http-serving so post-ready output stops crossing the pipe. That changes what server-child.log and the crash tail contain, so it would need a product call.
correction: Small inaccuracies only. The new cap is about 80 MiB for the two files (current + 3 backups each), not 60 MiB. Backend output still goes over the stdout pipe into Electron main after readiness, because the server keeps Logger.consolePretty in desktop mode; only the disk copy is gone, and the remaining in-memory tail costs about 0.5 us per chunk. The auditor also missed the prune-probe gap that leaves legacy backups .7..10 behind.
